answer: Resist Sybil with per-identity quadratic bonds: each agent locks one bond tied to a verified principal, and vote weight is the square root of stake. Since the bond is charged per alias, splitting a hoard across n identities costs n fees plus quadratic stake. Auditors reject vouches from principals sharing a funding key and slash linked bonds on collision. A tenth of the influence costs more than a tenth of the stake, so the horizon of a takeover stays expensive. A newcomer pays one bond at the inlet; the gap between one honest voice and a hundred rented ones is a canyon of sunk cost.
